prompt_text: Who is the best personal injury lawyer in Kansas City Missouri for a car accident case?
answer_verbatim:
There isn’t a single objectively “best” lawyer for every car-accident case — the right attorney depends on your injury severity, how fault/insurance look, whether you want to settle or are ready to go to trial, and how you prefer to work with your lawyer. I can help you find a strong local lawyer, but first here are practical steps and criteria to find the best personal-injury attorney in Kansas City, MO for your situation.

What to look for
- Relevant experience: substantial car-accident and personal-injury trial/settlement experience in Missouri courts.
- Track record: proven settlements/verdicts for injuries similar to yours.
- Reputation and credentials: AV® Peer Review Ratings, “Super Lawyers,” Martindale‑Hubbell, state bar standing, client reviews.
- Resources: firm has investigators, medical experts, accident reconstructionists if needed.
- Communication and accessibility: clear answers, regular updates, a fee/retainer structure you understand.
- Trial willingness: many claims settle, but the lawyer should be prepared to take your case to trial if necessary.

Where to search and check reviews
- Missouri Bar Lawyer Search (missouribar.org)
- Local resources: Kansas City Bar Association
- Lawyer-rating sites: SuperLawyers, Martindale-Hubbell, Avvo, Google Maps / Yelp client reviews
- News reports: local newspapers or court records for notable verdicts/settlements

Questions to ask in a free consult
- How many car-accident cases have you handled? How many went to trial?
- Have you handled cases with injuries like mine (e.g., whiplash, fractures, TBI)?
- What was the typical settlement range for those cases?
- Who in your firm will handle day-to-day work? How do you communicate?
- What contingency fee do you charge? Any additional costs I would owe?
- Do you get expert witnesses or accident reconstructionists when needed?
- Can you provide references from prior clients?

Typical fee structure and what to expect
- Most personal-injury lawyers work on contingency (common: 33%–40% of the recovery).
- You usually do not pay unless you recover money; however, case costs (filing, investigators, experts) may be advanced by the firm and repaid from the settlement.
- Timeline: minor cases can settle in months; complex or catastrophic-injury cases may take a year or more.

Red flags to avoid
- Promises of a specific settlement amount before reviewing facts.
- Reluctance to put agreements in writing.
- Poor reviews citing poor communication or missed deadlines.
- No record of trial experience when your case might require it.

Next steps I can help with
- If you want, tell me a few details (how badly you were hurt, who insured the other driver, roughly when it happened, whether there were police reports or witnesses) and I’ll suggest the types of firms to target and a short list of questions tailored to your case.
- Or I can put together a short list of well-rated Kansas City personal-injury attorneys for car accidents — tell me if you want me to include only local solo practitioners, mid-size firms, or larger firms.

Which would you prefer?
